summary:
Review of the proposed DFT campaign through the physics-and-method lens. PKG is C:\Users\moham\Downloads\IWO_Local_Codex_Handoff (1)\IWO_PHYSICS_CONSTRAINED_MODEL_V1. I only read files; nothing was run or changed.

The proposal uses the right DFT vocabulary. But two of its main premises are contradicted by the package itself.

1. **Contacts do not explain the off-state floors.** The idea that a Pd contact barrier, or oxygen vacancies (V_O) near Pd, explain the floors does not hold, for three reasons:
   - The floors do not change with gate voltage. A barrier in series with a gate-depleted channel can only lower the current.
   - The earlier Astra model already used a Schottky Pd contact (work function 4.45 eV plus SURF.REC). It still gave native zeros in the off state. Changing the emission coefficient changed the on-current by only 0.38 % and left all 54 zero points unchanged.
   - The floor ratios between thicknesses (x33 and x43) cannot follow an exp(-dPhi/kT) law driven by confinement.

2. **DFT at 6.3 and 13.2 nm is not worth running.**
   - The expected confinement difference there is 0.02-0.05 eV. This is no larger than the DFT noise.
   - A simple effective-mass estimate already gives it.
   - Consistent relaxed cells (about 500 and about 1056 atoms) are estimated at 250 GB to over 1 TB of memory. That is beyond one H100.
   - Crystalline slabs cannot address the x4.6 mobility step in any case.

The useful core is smaller than proposed:
- finish the 2 nm slab;
- split the gap opening between conduction and valence band. The hybrid-functional (HSE) part of this can be read from outputs that already exist: in bulk, HSE minus PBE gives about -1.01 eV on the valence-band edge and +0.12 to +0.17 eV on the conduction-band edge. At 1 nm, HSE adds about 0.06 eV to the conduction-band shift (computed here, not validated);
- resolve the unexplained 1.1-1.65 eV vacuum-level shift of the W-doped 1 nm slab before any doped-slab alignment is trusted;
- test W-5d localization in bulk, with dilution and with HSE;
- compute bulk V_O formation energies and charge transition levels with HSE and finite-size corrections, reported over the full oxygen chemical-potential range because the growth conditions are unknown;
- add a 3 nm slab instead of 6.3 and 13.2 nm;
- treat the Pd contact in stages, starting with a cheap bulk branch-point estimate.

The amorphous models, the Al2O3 interface models, the full stack and most of the Pd/W/V_O interface jobs should be dropped or deferred. They are unaffordable, or they cannot be identified from one transfer curve per film, or both.

All cost and size figures here are labelled estimates scaled from the measured costs. Any TCAD check needs new ATLAS launches, which require the user's approval (57 of 57 used).

findings.item: Premise of Block 1 and Block 2: a Pd/IWO barrier or V_O near Pd as the origin of the off-state floors, checked by 'DFT Phi_Bn -> freeze in TCAD -> predict I_off'
findings.detail: (1) The floors are flat, gate-independent plateaus. The 13.2 nm floor stays within x1.06 while V_gd goes from 1.2 to 3.7 V. In the off state the channel is depleted by the gate, and any contact barrier is in series with it, so a lower barrier cannot raise a gate-independent floor. Drift-diffusion gives native zeros there whatever the contact. (2) The claim that changing the contact potential brought the simulated off-current toward measurement is contradicted. The Astra lineage used Schottky S/D contacts (work function 4.45 eV plus SURF.REC, about 0.15 eV effective barrier) and still had native zeros: 54/54/46 points. Its Schottky two-carrier control gave off-window |Id| of about 1e-34 to 1e-54 A/um. The contact-emission sensitivity changed I_on by 0.381 % and left all 54 zero samples unchanged. (3) Thickness scaling: the floors are 4.61e-15, 1.53e-13 and 6.60e-12 A/um, so the steps are x33.2 and x43.1. These need kT ln(ratio) = 0.091 and 0.097 eV of barrier change. The V1 confinement law gives 0.281 eV between 2 and 6.3 nm, which predicts x5.3e4, and S3 allows at most 0.05 eV between 6.3 and 13.2 nm, which gives at most x7. An exp(-dPhi/kT) law fails both steps (computed here, conditional on the model). (4) The thermionic factors 48x and 2.3e3x are arithmetically correct at 300 K, but they apply only to contact-limited current. (5) Physics risk: a DFT barrier change of 0.1-0.2 eV is the same size as the HSE correction to the conduction-band edge (+0.12 to +0.17 eV, below) and as the expected spread over interface registry and termination. An apparent match would therefore be coincidental. If contacts are still of interest, the observables are on-state and low-Vd ones (the registered ID-VD ratios; an S-shape or Id(0.1)/Id(0.05) > 2.0 at 2 nm). These need new lab data. Any ATLAS test also needs launches beyond 57 of 57.

findings.item: Item 1: relaxed 2 nm pristine slab (Eg, EC/EV, m*, DOS, vacuum level; PBE plus HSE check)
findings.verdict: KEEP (already running); MODIFY the HSE part, the mass read-out and the thickness definition
findings.detail: slab2_relax_c2 was at 40 BFGS steps after 23 h. The lost first run reached a gap of 1.22 eV (+0.33 eV, provisional), matching Lin et al.'s +0.33 eV. HSE on the 2 nm slab should not be planned. Its exact-exchange arrays are estimated at 40.6 GB x (176/96)^2 ≈ 136 GB, more than the 94 GB of the H100. Its run time is estimated at 16-25 h, which sits at the ~25 h Kerberos/EOS checkpoint limit. Transfer the 1 nm HSE/PBE ratio of 1.06-1.11 instead. If a 2 nm HSE run is still wanted, first show on the 1 nm slab that reduced settings (ecutfock 120 Ry, Gamma-only exchange) reproduce the ratio 1.060 within ±0.02 (pre-register this). There are no HSE masses from bands, because pw.x has no hybrid non-SCF bands. Get the HSE/PBE mass ratio only for the 40-atom bulk, using an HSE SCF with extra zero-weight k-points within 0.05 1/A of Gamma, and keep the PBE mass increment. Check with projwfc layer projections that the CBM and VBM states are delocalized through the slab and are not surface O-H states. The unrelaxed 1 nm slab had its VBM off Gamma and dEg = 0.07 eV, against 0.90 eV after relaxation. Fix the thickness definition before refitting the law: the 2 nm slab is 18.34 A between outer O layers and 20.18 A between outer H atoms (as built). With dEc ∝ t^-1.38, a 10 % ambiguity in t gives about 14 % (about 0.05 eV) at 2 nm (estimate).

findings.item: Item 2: vacuum alignment of bulk, 1 nm and 2 nm (EA, IP, dEc, dEv; PBE plus hybrid correction)
findings.verdict: KEEP (highest TCAD value); MODIFY the method
findings.detail:
The deck sets AFFINITY = chi_bulk - dEc with dEc = dEg, i.e. it assumes the valence-band edge does not move. It solves for electrons only (carriers=1). So only dEc matters for TCAD, and the partition decides it. Method: (i) dEc(1) - dEc(2) = EA(2) - EA(1), and the same for IP, using slabs with the same termination (PBE, PAW). This is robust, because absolute EA and IP contain a termination dipole. (ii) For the bulk reference, use the two-step macroscopic-average alignment on the interior of the 2 nm (and 3 nm) slab. Averaging window: a/4 = 2.577 A. Pre-register that the macroscopic average must be flat within ±20 meV over at least one period. The 1 nm slab (7.88 A between outer O layers) has no bulk-like interior and must not be aligned to bulk directly. Compute the bulk reference at the slab's in-plane lattice (10.336 vs 10.306 A) to remove strain. (iii) The HSE correction is mostly available already in existing outputs (computed here from Kohn-Sham edges relative to the cell-average electrostatic potential, NC SG15, same geometries; not validated):
- Bulk, HSE minus PBE: VBM -1.015 eV, CBM +0.173 eV at q=1 (-1.024 / +0.122 eV at q=3).
- 1 nm slab: VBM -1.008 eV, CBM +0.233 eV at q=1.
- So HSE adds about +0.060 eV to dEc and about -0.007 eV to dEv at 1 nm. The sum, 0.053 eV, equals the reported dEg difference.
- About 85 % of the PBE gap error sits in the VBM.
Confirm the reference convention with pp.x planar averages of the HSE runs before using these numbers.

findings.item: ADD (blocking): resolve the unexplained 1.1-1.65 eV vacuum-scale shift of the W-doped 1 nm slab before any doped-slab alignment or barrier
findings.detail: With one W, every level of the 1 nm slab moves up on the vacuum scale: the valence top by 1.65 eV and the host CB by 1.27 eV, and E_vac minus band 313 drops from 3.93 to 2.85 eV. The cause is not determined. Simple electrostatics predicts the opposite sign: a positive W donor at the centre with its electrons spread outward should move the levels down, i.e. raise EA (my inference). So a read-out or reference error must be excluded first. Candidates: the vacuum window, Gamma-only levels vs the full-k-grid edges used for the pure slab, the smearing reference. Diagnostic: at the same geometry (W substituted into the pure relaxed slab, before relaxation), compute dV(z) = V_IWO - V_pure and drho(z) with pp.x and average.x. Then compute the dipole and quadrupole moments of drho. Whatever the cause, 3 electrons per 107 A^2 (2.8e14 cm^-2) can produce eV-scale electrostatic shifts (order-of-magnitude estimate). Absolute alignments of doped 1x1 slabs are therefore not transferable to the device.

findings.item: Item 3: 2 nm IWO slab with W at the centre (PDOS, W-5d, E_F, charge transfer, m*)
Items 4-5: W subsurface and W at the surface (segregation)
findings.detail:
Definition: E_seg(i) = E(W at depth i) - E(W at centre). Negative means W prefers depth i. Use the same composition and the same cell (atoms relaxed at the pristine relaxed in-plane cell, no vc-relax), the same k grid, smearing, cutoffs and nbnd. Five fixes:
(a) Site type. The bulk 8b-24d difference of 0.258 eV is likely larger than the segregation energy. Compare 24d with 24d at every depth (the central layer holds only 24d) and 8b separately.
(b) Symmetry. A single W on one side breaks the z -> -z operation and creates a dipole. Use symmetric pairs (one W per surface vs two W in the central layer, same composition), or a Bengtsson dipole correction (tefield/dipfield, edir=3, emaxpos in vacuum). make_jobs.py has no switch for this.
(c) Hydrogen. The 'surface' is the fully hydroxylated O layer. A W6+ next to OH may deprotonate. Test variants with 1-3 H removed. These change the composition, so report them as a function of mu_H (H2/H2O references).
(d) Periodic images. Check 1x1 against 2x1 for the lowest configuration on the 1 nm slab (192 atoms).
(e) Kinetics. The only anneal is 150 °C for 600 s, so equilibrium segregation gives a driving force only. The W profile is set during sputtering and is not determined. The occupation ratio of 430:1 quoted for 600 K is for a hypothetical temperature.

findings.item: Items 6-8: V_O in the 2 nm slab (interior, subsurface, surface)
findings.detail:
(a) Bookkeeping. All 24 surface O carry an H, so a 'surface V_O' is not defined until the H is accounted for. Removing O and keeping H, removing OH (V_OH, 1 electron) and removing H2O (O + 2H, 0 electrons) are different defects. Specify each one and compare only at the same composition.
(b) Physics risk. In PBE (gap 0.9-1.8 eV) the neutral V_O state may be resonant with the CB, which delocalizes it artificially. Its 2 electrons per 107 A^2 (1.9e14 cm^-2) are degenerate.
(c) Use energies relative to other positions inside one slab; formation energies against bulk need mu_O.
(d) Use symmetric pairs or a dipole correction for off-centre vacancies.
(e) The question 'can V_O explain carrier density / off-state' cannot be answered. Concentrations need mu_O and the kinetics, which are NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA, and the floors are not channel-limited (first finding). Reframe it as: is V_O shallow or deep at 2 nm compared with bulk, using HSE-corrected edges. Postpone charged defects in slabs. They need Komsa-Pasquarello or Freysoldt-Neugebauer-type slab corrections, or the QE ESM/gate options.

findings.item: Items 9-10: W+V_O adjacent and separated
findings.detail: E_bind = E(W) + E(V_O) - E(W+V_O) - E(pristine) is balanced in composition: each side has one W and one missing O, so no chemical potentials enter. Positive means bound. All four runs must use the identical cell, k grid and occupations, so run the pristine slab with the same MV smearing rather than fixed occupations. Physics: W6+ and V_O are both donors (5 extra electrons in the neutral cell), so 'passivation' is the wrong picture. When ionized they should repel. The motivation that W suppresses V_O (Januar, used only as motivation in the report) more plausibly works through the Fermi level: the formation energy of V_O^2+ rises by 2 dE_F when W raises E_F. Neutral same-cell energies do not capture this; the bulk charged-defect route below does. Item 10 tests distance, not concentration, because the concentration is the same in the same cell. Use at least 3 separations, in a 2x1 cell or in the 160-atom bulk cell.

findings.item: Bulk V_O^q formation energies and transition levels (Block 1 recommendation)
findings.detail:
Method:
- Cell: the 80-atom conventional cell, with a 160-atom check.
- Charge states q = 0, +1 (spin-polarized), +2, each relaxed with PBE.
- HSE06 single points with SG15 NC In/O at the PBE geometries. This misses the HSE relaxation energy; label that.
- Finite-size correction: FNV or Kumagai-Oba (method references, not bundled). Bracket with eps0 = 9.30 (C-V) and 10.55 (literature), eps_inf = 4.05, and include the potential alignment.
- Chemical potentials over the full range from In-rich to O-rich: 2mu_In + 3mu_O = dH_f(In2O3), mu_O ≤ 1/2 E(O2) with a stated correction for PBE O2 overbinding; W bounded by WO3, H by H2O.
- Read the transition levels against the HSE CBM.
Growth conditions (sputter O2 pressure, anneal ambient) are not in the package. Report every result against mu_O and claim nothing that holds only in part of the range. Concentrations and N_D: NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA. Cost (estimate): PBE relax about 10-24 h on 32 cores per charge state, scaled from the W cells; HSE single point about 1-3 GPU-h each.

findings.item: Item 11: Pd on 2 nm pristine In2O3 (Phi_B, interface dipole, drho(z), LDOS)
findings.verdict: MODIFY (staged; explicit interface only if a pre-registered trigger is met)
findings.detail:
Stage 0 (cheap):
- Compute the bulk branch-point energy (Brillouin-zone-averaged mid-gap energy, Tersoff/Mönch type; method references not bundled) from the existing PBE bulk bands, with the HSE edge corrections above. Report the spread from the band-count convention.
- The package literature puts the charge-neutrality level about 0.4 eV above E_c, which supports a pinned Ohmic contact.
- Compute the Pd work function from a 5-7-layer Pd slab. This gives only a weak Schottky-Mott bound, because EA depends on termination.
- Pre-register a trigger: build the explicit interface only if the branch point minus the HSE CBM is below +0.1 eV.
Stage 1 (interface):
- Oxide at least 2 nm, 3 nm preferred. MIGS decay is about 0.3-1 nm (estimate), longer in PBE, so the 1 nm oxide has no bulk-like region.
- Pd at least 5 layers; 5 vs 7 layers must agree within 0.05 eV. A 4x4 Pd(001) net on 10.31 A is about -6 % strain in Pd (handbook Pd lattice constant; not in the package). Report the Pd work function against strain and check nspin=2.
- Contact-side terminations: O-terminated (12 H removed, so 12 holes per cell are filled by Pd), OH-retained, and reduced/In-rich. At least 2 lateral registries each. Rank them by interface energy against mu_O and mu_H.
- Dipole correction is mandatory (asymmetric slab). Test k-point grids from 6x6x1 upward.
Extraction:
- Phi_Bn = [E_CBM - Vbar]_bulk (HSE, strained to the slab in-plane lattice) + Vbar(oxide interior) - E_F.
- Cross-check with layer PDOS where the MIGS have decayed.
- drho(z) = rho_int - rho_Pd - rho_ox at frozen positions.
- Apply the hybrid correction through the bulk CBM shift (+0.12 to +0.17 eV), assuming the PBE interface dipole is right; at 1 nm the shift is +0.23 eV, so the correction depends on thickness.
Pd and Al PAW/SG15 pseudopotentials are not in the package; downloading them needs user approval, then a cutoff test. Size and cost (estimate): about 280-290 atoms and at least 2400 electrons with a metallic k grid, about 200-370 GB of host memory, and per-SCF cost an order of magnitude or more above the 2 nm slab. Search registries on a 1 nm oxide and do single points on 2-3 nm. TCAD mapping: CONTACT WORKFUN = chi + Phi_Bn for an unconfined (metallized) film under Pd, with chi(t) in the channel, so that the lateral barrier Phi_Bn + dEc(t) emerges in ATLAS. This needs approved launches.
findings.evidence: PKG\analysis_2026-09-25\S5_contacts_experimental_validation.md:47-51; PKG\decks\full_physical_structure.in:29,62-65; PKG\qe_workflow\pseudo (only In/O/H/W PAW and In/O/H/W ONCV); PKG\qe_workflow\cern_htcondor\PROTOCOL_CERN.md:181; PKG\report_latex_full\chapters\13_dft.tex:1256-1258; PKG\report_latex_full\chapters\09_mechanisms.tex:211-215,223-224

findings.item: Items 12-13 and the Block 2 mini-campaign (Pd/IWO, Pd/IWO + interfacial V_O at three depths, Pd/IWO + W+V_O)
findings.verdict: DROP (defer at most one V_O-at-interface run after item 11)
findings.detail: A 1x1 W-doped cell puts a donor sheet of about 2.8e14 cm^-2 against the Pd. That screens any barrier within the first layer, so a W-induced change of Phi_Bn would be an artefact of the doping level. A V_O next to Pd ionizes, and its interface dipole lowers the barrier by dPhi = N_s p / eps. The DFT cell fixes N_s at one per 107 A^2 (9.4e13 cm^-2), while the real areal density is NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA. If one run is kept, extract only the dipole per vacancy p and the charge state, and leave N_s as an explicit unknown. Trap-assisted tunnelling from Pd through a defect into the IWO CB needs an insulating barrier, and none exists between Pd and IWO. Compare formation energies of V_O at the interface and in the oxide interior only within one Pd/oxide cell, at the Fermi level set by the metal. The motivating off-current link is falsified (first finding).

findings.item: Items 14-15: Al2O3/2 nm IWO, with and without V_O
findings.detail: The Al2O3 is 2 nm of ALD oxide grown at 250 °C, i.e. amorphous. Crystalline interface models impose a large lattice mismatch with bixbyite (10.31 A) and arbitrary registry choices, so the band offsets come with uncertainties of several tenths of an eV (estimate). Their outputs map onto chi, Q_f and V_FB, which are degenerate in the TCAD: ±0.2 eV of alignment equals ±1.12e12 cm^-2 of Q_f. Without per-thickness C-V V_FB data there is no test that can identify them. No Al pseudopotential is in the package. The only physics value is the finite barrier that limits confinement at 1-2 nm. Bound it with an effective-mass calculation over a range of conduction-band offsets; the offset value is NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA.

findings.item: Item 16: full Pd/IWO/Al2O3 local stack
findings.detail: It combines every uncertainty of items 11 and 14. It would have over 500 atoms with a metallic k grid (estimate), which does not fit on one GPU, and multi-GPU requests waited hours. It has no identifiable TCAD observable.

findings.item: Items 17-20: three amorphous 2 nm IWO models (AIMD melt-quench) plus one with V_O
findings.verdict: DROP for this campaign (DEFER until structural data exist)
findings.detail: Size and statistics: at least 200-300 atoms per film model, and at least 5 independent quenches are needed for tail statistics; 3 is too few. AIMD quench rates of about 1e13-1e15 K/s far exceed sputter conditions and over-disorder the structure. Validation needs film density (XRR) and coordination/RDF (EXAFS) of the target films: NOT DETERMINED FROM AVAILABLE DATA. PBE delocalization makes tail states look too extended (IPR biased), and the gap is compressed. Cost (estimate): 10k-20k MD steps at about 2.5-11 min per step for ~250 atoms (Gamma-only, cutoff 45-71 Ry) gives about 450-1800 GPU-h per sample, against 85-90 GPU-h used so far. The 6.3 to 13.2 nm question concerns crystallinity, grain coalescence and percolation at 6-13 nm, which no DFT cell of this size can represent. If revived: melt-quench bulk a-IWO with a validated machine-learned or classical potential, take DFT single points of the snapshots, HSE on 1-2 of them, and extract a mobility edge from the IPR.

findings.item: Item 21: about 3 nm pristine film as a bridge point
findings.verdict: KEEP (recommended instead of DFT at 6.3/13.2 nm)
findings.detail: Build it by inserting one relaxed-bulk conventional cell into the centre of the relaxed 2 nm slab: In88O144H24, 256 atoms, 2032 electrons, charge-balanced. This starts close to convergence. Do not use the legacy qe_workflow\slab_3p0nm_In2O3 input: H16In96O144 gives 3x96 + 16 = 304 ≠ 2x144 = 288, so it is metallic (smearing, tefield), and the README marks it NOT EXECUTED. The expected shift is about 0.19 eV (S3, DFT-anchored), well above the noise. It fixes the exponent of the thickness law, and a Kane effective-mass model calibrated on 1/2/3 nm then gives 6.3 and 13.2 nm. Cost (estimate): relax about 66 GB host memory, 81-105 min per BFGS step, 40-120 GPU-h. The final SCF with +16 bands would need about 140 GB, so use +8 bands or CPUs. Runs longer than 25 h depend on the laptop snapshot loop.

findings.item: Item 22: second W concentration
findings.detail: First compare the 160-atom 1x1x2 bulk cell (In63WO96, 1.6 % W) with the 80-atom cell (3.1 %). Measure the W-5d weight at E_F, the magnetic moment and E_F - CBM. Then run HSE06 (SG15 W is available) on the 80-atom W24d cell. Metallic, with smearing; estimate 2-6 GPU-h. This is the decisive test of whether the W-5d localization is a PBE effect or a W-W image effect at 10.3 A. Use a slab 2x1 cell only if the bulk result changes with dilution. Rebuild the 160-atom cell with the structures_v2 checks; the legacy bulk_IWO_1W_1p6pct_112 directory is not executed. The composition basis of '~2 % W' is undefined, so concentrations should bracket rather than match it.

findings.item: Block 3: DFT for the 6.3 nm and 13.2 nm devices
findings.detail:
Effective-mass estimate (computed here): the infinite-well E1 with m* = 0.208 is 0.046 eV at 6.3 nm and 0.010 eV at 13.2 nm. S3 gives 0.02-0.05 eV and <0.02 eV. The mass law gives +0.010 vs +0.003 m0, a ratio of 1.03, which cannot produce x4.6 in mobility for any mu ∝ m*^-n with n ≤ 2.5. That negative result is therefore already established, and the report already rejects confinement for this step.
Noise: these signals sit at the level of the DFT noise — NC vs PAW dEg 14 meV, HSE ratio ±5 %, strain from the in-plane relaxation (10.336 vs 10.306 A), surface-state edges, forces at 1e-3 Ry/bohr.
Consistency: relaxation moved the 1 nm dEg from 0.07 to 0.90 eV, so unrelaxed 'baseline' single points would not be comparable.
Size (recipe): 6.3 nm gives 496 atoms and 13.2 nm 1056. Estimated host memory is about 250-520 GB and 1.1-2.4 TB. Estimated time is 6-13 h and 35-120 h per BFGS step, i.e. 430-890 GPU-h for 6.3 nm if the memory fitted. That is infeasible.
Scope: crystalline (001) slabs contain no grain boundaries, disorder or percolation, so they cannot address the mobility jump; GIXRD/TEM, gated Hall and temperature data can.

findings.item: HSE06 on only 5-7 decisive systems
findings.verdict: MODIFY (feasible list; norm-conserving only; no metallic interfaces)

findings.item: Bader charges
findings.detail:
Neither the package nor QE has a Bader code. Use instead:
- the Löwdin charges and spilling parameter that projwfc.x already prints (projwfc is in the driver). Use only differences between configurations of the same cell.
- planar-integrated drho(z) and its dipole moment, which do not depend on a basis, as the primary measure of charge transfer.
If Bader is wanted: install the external code (needs user approval), run it on pp.x cube files of the PAW all-electron density (plot_num=21, not the valence pseudo-density) on the fine FFT grid, and report only differences. Absolute Bader or Löwdin charges in In2O3 are far from the formal ionic values.

findings.item: ADD: termination sensitivity and the air-exposed back surface
findings.detail: The symmetric slab with one H per surface O is a model; the device has Al2O3 below and air (OH, H2O, O2; ambient not recorded) above. The 1 nm dEg changed from 0.07 to 0.90 eV on relaxation, so the DFT confinement at 1-2 nm depends strongly on structure and termination. Before refitting the law, test termination sensitivity on the 1 nm slab with two variants. The first is an adsorbed H2O layer on the OH surface, which is neutral and leaves the electron count unchanged. The second is an asymmetric OH/O variant with dipole correction. Pre-register: dEc must change by less than 0.05 eV, otherwise carry the spread as an uncertainty. Adsorbate densities are unknown, so nothing maps to TCAD charge; the back-charge hypothesis A3 was rejected as the sole cause.

findings.item: DFT-to-TCAD mapping table
findings.detail:
- dEc(t) -> AFFINITY(t): yes. Eg(t) matters little, because holes are not solved.
- m*(t) -> N_C(t): approximate, since a 2D in-plane DOS mass goes into a 3D continuum N_C.
- Phi_Bn -> contact boundary condition: ATLAS CONTACT WORKFUN = chi + Phi_Bn, with SURF.REC/E.TUNNEL, a fine mesh under the contact, and an explicit choice of chi for the IWO under Pd.
- V_O/W -> N_D: no. DFT cannot give concentrations, so N_D stays fitted.
- Interface dipole -> Q_f/V_FB: degenerate with WF, chi and Q_f, so it cannot be identified.
- Defect DOS -> g_t(E): no. Crystalline defect bands at about 1e14 cm^-2 are not an exponential tail (W_TA = 40 meV), and only dilute HSE levels are meaningful.
Every TCAD use needs new ATLAS launches (57 of 57 used), which need the user's approval.

findings.item: ADD: workflow prerequisites for the new physics

top_recommendations: Drop the off-current motivation for the Pd/V_O work. The floors do not change with gate voltage, a Schottky Pd contact was already tested in the Astra lineage and left the native off-state zeros unchanged, and the x33/x43 floor steps do not follow exp(-dPhi/kT). Any contact study should target on-state and low-Vd observables, which need lab data.

Finish the 2 nm slab without an HSE run on it (estimated 136 GB of exact-exchange arrays); transfer the 1 nm ratio of 1.06-1.11. Fix and pre-register the film-thickness definition before refitting dEc(t), because a 10 % ambiguity in t moves the 2 nm value by about 0.05 eV.

Split the gap opening between conduction and valence band using the EA differences of slabs with the same termination, plus a bulk reference aligned on the slab interior at the slab in-plane lattice. Take the HSE correction from existing outputs: bulk VBM -1.015 eV / CBM +0.173 eV, and at 1 nm HSE adds +0.060 eV to dEc (computed here, not validated; confirm with planar averages of the HSE runs).

Before trusting any W-doped slab alignment or barrier, resolve the unexplained 1.1-1.65 eV vacuum-scale shift of the 1 nm IWO slab (same-geometry dV(z) and drho(z)). Simple electrostatics predicts the opposite sign, so check the read-out first.

Test W-5d localization in bulk before any more slabs: compare 160 atoms (1.6 % W) with 80 atoms (3.1 %), run a spin-polarized check, then HSE06 (NC) on the 80-atom W24d cell. Then run the chained 2 nm IWO slab, reading only local quantities, with donor depth vs thickness as the main question.
